quizName: DMV Practice Test #15 16 Questions • Passing Score 12

questions.question: If you cannot avoid hitting an object in the road, you should:

options.text: Speed up before you hit it.
Slow down before you hit it.
Lean the motorcycle.
Stay seated on the motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down before you hit it.
questions.explanation: If you cannot avoid hitting an object, try to hit it at a 90-degree angle. Slow down as much as you can before impact. Keep your motorcycle upright. Rise slightly off your seat. Roll the throttle gently to lighten the front end just before you hit the object.

questions.question: As a rider, you should prepare a passenger by instructing them to do all of the following, except:

options.text: Get on the motorcycle after the engine starts.
Sit as far forward as possible.
Keep a large space between themselves and you.
Keep their legs away from the muffler and chains.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep a large space between themselves and you.
questions.explanation: Before riding, ask your passenger to mount the motorcycle only after the engine starts. They should sit as far forward as they can without crowding you. They should hold the passenger handholds or your waist, hips, or belt. They should keep their legs away from the muffler, chains, and other moving parts.

questions.question: When following a car, ride in which part of the lane?

options.text: The left portion.
The center portion.
The right portion.
The left or right portions.

questions.explanation: Ride in the center of the lane when following a car. The driver will see you in their rearview mirror. Most drivers check their rearview mirrors more often than their side mirrors. This position helps you be seen.

questions.question: A rectangular sign could be a:

options.text: School crossing sign.
Railroad crossing sign.
Stop sign.
Speed limit sign.

questions.explanation: Regulatory signs, like speed limit signs, are rectangular with white background and black lettering. You must follow the rules posted on these signs.

questions.question: How can you stop another vehicle from sharing your lane?

options.text: Ride in the middle of your lane.
Ride in the left portion of your lane.
Ride in the right portion of your lane.
Swerve from side to side in your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride in the middle of your lane.
questions.explanation: Ride in the center of your lane. This discourages other drivers from trying to share your lane.

questions.question: For eye or face shield protection to work well, it must be all of the following, except:

options.text: Able to fasten securely.
Too tight to allow sunglasses or eyeglasses to be worn.
Free of scratches.
Able to allow clear views to both sides.

questions.correctAnswerText: Too tight to allow sunglasses or eyeglasses to be worn.
questions.explanation: A good eye or face shield must be free of scratches, resist damage, allow clear side views, fasten securely, let air pass through to prevent fogging, and allow room for eyeglasses or sunglasses if needed.

questions.question: Which is a bad reason to use your horn?

options.text: A driver next to you is following the vehicle ahead too closely.
A parked car has someone in the driver's seat.
You want people to notice your motorcycle.
You are passing someone in the street.

questions.correctAnswerText: You want people to notice your motorcycle.
questions.explanation: Use your horn when passing a vehicle or person who might move into your lane. If a driver is following too closely, they may try to pass and cut in front of you. If someone is in a parked car or in the street, sound your horn as you pass to alert them.

questions.question: To control a motorcycle best, a rider should:

options.text: Sit with their arms fully extended.
Use their arms to hold their body up.
Keep their knees away from the gas tank.
Keep their feet firmly on the footrests.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep their feet firmly on the footrests.
questions.explanation: Sit so you can use your arms to control the motorcycle, not to hold yourself up. Your arms should be slightly bent at the handgrips. Keep your knees against the gas tank and your feet firmly on the footrests for balance.

questions.question: A good lane position should do all of the following, except:

options.text: Help you set up for turns.
Give you an escape route.
Help you avoid wind from other vehicles.
Place you in another vehicle's blind spot.

questions.correctAnswerText: Place you in another vehicle's blind spot.
questions.explanation: A good lane position increases your visibility and helps you see others. It helps you avoid wind blasts, blind spots, and road hazards. Your lane position should discourage other drivers from sharing your lane and give you an escape route if a hazard appears.

questions.question: When riding in a group, riders should:

options.text: Spread out to make the group easier to see.
Stay close together to make the group easier to see.
Separate occasionally.
Ride in pairs.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay close together to make the group easier to see.
questions.explanation: Keep the group close together while leaving enough space for each rider to maneuver. Staying close makes the group easier to see and prevents riders from separating. Pairs do not allow enough room to maneuver safely.

questions.question: How should you pack a load on a motorcycle?

options.text: Put heavier items toward the front.
Put heavier items toward the rear.
Mount loads behind the rear axle.
Store lighter items in front of you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Put heavier items toward the front.
questions.explanation: Place heavier items toward the front of the load. Loads should sit over or in front of the rear axle. Pack lighter items behind you.

questions.question: When braking on a slippery surface, what should you do?

options.text: Use only the rear brake.
Use only the front brake.
Use both brakes.
Do not use brakes. Downshift instead.

questions.explanation: On slippery surfaces, slow down and avoid sudden movements. Use both brakes when you need to slow down or stop.

questions.question: In a group ride, where should inexperienced riders position themselves?

options.text: Just behind the leader.
In front of the group.
At the end of the group.
Beside the leader.

questions.explanation: Inexperienced riders should ride just behind the leader. This lets experienced riders watch them without making the new rider lead the group.

questions.question: A driver is tailgating you. What should you do?

options.text: Flash your brake light before slowing down to warn them.
Speed up.
Pull to the side of the road.
Slow down.

questions.correctAnswerText: Flash your brake light before slowing down to warn them.
questions.explanation: Flash your brake light before slowing down when someone is tailgating. They may be focused on you and not see hazards ahead that require everyone to slow down.

questions.question: How often should you check a motorcycle's hydraulic fluid at minimum?

options.text: Once a day
Once a week
Once a year
Before every ride

questions.explanation: Before each ride, inspect your motorcycle. Check hydraulic fluids and coolants at least once a week for safe riding.

questions.question: Which of these does NOT affect blood alcohol content (BAC)?

options.text: The amount of alcohol consumed
How fast the alcohol is consumed
The drinker's body weight
How often the drinker drinks alcohol

questions.correctAnswerText: How often the drinker drinks alcohol
questions.explanation: Three factors affect BAC: the amount of alcohol consumed, how fast it was consumed, and body weight. Drinking and driving is illegal and dangerous.
